fields.note: A search summary quoted the guide: 'The dimensions of the 2024 Porsche 911 are a wheelbase of 96.5 inches, length of 177.9 inches and width of 72.9 inches.' CAUTION: the earlier card review found this same guide carried a 3,311 lb weight and implausible performance figures. No Porsche dimension sheet surfaced. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Stuttcars' '2020 Porsche 911 Carrera (992) Technical Specifications' page: 'Track width front (inches/mm) | 62.7 in. / 1591 mm'. Model year 2020 base Carrera (992.1, same 379 hp RWD PDK car as the 2024). A later summary said one CarExpert 2024 Carrera page also showed 1,591 mm front track (page not identified). A 992.2 Carrera S listing gives 1,601 mm, a different car. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Stuttcars' '2020 Porsche 911 Carrera (992) Technical Specifications' page: 'Track width rear (inches/mm) | 61.2 in. / 1557 mm'. Model year 2020 base Carrera (992.1). Same buyer's-guide sentence as wheelbaseIn: 'length of 177.9 inches'. The summary said another result 'independently lists the length at 177.9 inches' without naming it. Model-wide, not trim-specific; see the caution on wheelbaseIn about this guide. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

Same buyer's-guide sentence: 'width of 72.9 inches'. Autoblog's 2020 Carrera Cabriolet page lists a 72.9-in body width, and a Porsche newsroom result gave the Carrera S Cabriolet's rear body width as 1,852 mm (72.91 in). Whether mirrors are included was not stated (72.9 in reads as body width without mirrors). Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

'The height of the 2024 Porsche 911 is 50.9 inches.' The only height figure found; trim and suspension not stated. See the caution on wheelbaseIn about this guide. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

A search summary said: 'The base Carrera's US spec sheet lists a curb weight of 3354 lbs, which is a manufacturer figure'; the Porsche sheet in that result list was '2020 911 Carrera and 911 Carrera Cabriolet US specifications' (model year 2020, same 992.1 PDK car). The line itself was not quoted, so the coupe column could not be confirmed. Cars.com lists a base curb weight of 3,354 lb for the 2024 Carrera Coupe and Edmunds matches it (carried from the card research, where the reviewer also saw 3,354 lb on Carwhere). Other listings in conflicts. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

A search summary said CarExpert's 2024 911 Carrera (RWD coupe, Australian market) listing gives 'Ground Clearance Unladen (mm): 121', which the summary converted to about 4.8 in. The summary did not say which of CarExpert's several 2024 Carrera pages carried it. LOW CONFIDENCE: the earlier card research saw 121 mm attributed to the Carrera in one summary and to the Carrera T in another and left it out (see conflicts). Suspension (steel or PASM) not stated. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

fields.publisher: Porsche (2020 911 Carrera S and Carrera 4S US specifications)
fields.note: TRIM CAUTION. The summary of Porsche's 2020 US sheet for the base 911 Carrera showed 'Transmission: Number of gears 8 ... 1st 4.89 4.89, 2nd 3.17 3.17' and was cut off after second gear. The full set (3rd 2.15, 4th 1.56, 5th 1.18, 6th 0.94, 7th 0.76, 8th 0.61, reverse 3.99) came from Porsche's 2020 Carrera S / Carrera 4S US sheet. The same eight ratios appeared on Stuttcars listings for a Carrera 4S PDK, a Carrera 4S Cabriolet and a 992.2 Carrera S. Third to eighth gear were therefore not seen for the base Carrera itself; they are recorded because the base sheet's first and second gears match and every 992 8-speed PDK listing seen carried the same ratios. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.

fields.publisher: Car and Driver (syndicated on Yahoo Autos)
fields.note: The Yahoo Autos page 'Tested: Base 2020 Porsche 911 Is a Worthy Six-Figure Sports Car' reports 'consistent, repeated passes of 3.2 seconds to 60 mph and 11.5 seconds through the quarter-mile' with the PDK automatic; the summary did not name the publisher on that page. A second summary (Stuttcars' 992.1 Carrera Coupe page) said 'Car and Driver's base, rear-drive Carrera (same 379-hp engine) repeatedly clocked 3.2 s to 60 mph and 11.5 s quarter-mile', which is the basis for naming Car and Driver. Test car: a model-year 2020 base Carrera coupe, 379 hp, 8-speed PDK, rear-wheel drive, the same configuration as the 2024 Carrera (the 992.1 Carrera ran unchanged in rating from 2020 to 2024 per the card research). Options on the test car (Sport Chrono launch control, tyres) were not stated. Porsche claims 4.0 s (3.8 s with Sport Chrono). The page mentions a December 2020 update with results for a PDK Carrera. Read from search-result summary; page not opened.
